gloss: the press corps; reporters on the scene

definitions.gloss: the press corps; the assembled reporters and camera crews
definitions.explanation: The body of journalists, photographers, and camera crews gathered to cover an event. Treated as a single collective group, so it is used with verbs like {囲|かこ}む (surround) and {詰|つ}めかける (throng).

examples.japanese: {報道陣|ほうどうじん}が{詰|つ}めかけた。
examples.english: The press corps thronged the place.

examples.japanese: {選手|せんしゅ}は{報道陣|ほうどうじん}に{囲|かこ}まれて{質問|しつもん}に{答|こた}えた。
examples.english: Surrounded by reporters, the athlete answered questions.

examples.japanese: {事故|じこ}の{現場|げんば}には{早朝|そうちょう}から{多|おお}くの{報道陣|ほうどうじん}が{集|あつ}まっていた。
examples.english: A large press corps had gathered at the accident site from early morning.

notes:
Formed from {報道|ほうどう} (news reporting) plus the suffix 〜{陣|じん}, which turns a field of activity into the body of people staffing it.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {報道陣|ほうどうじん}に{囲|かこ}まれる: to be surrounded by reporters
- {報道陣|ほうどうじん}が{詰|つ}めかける: the press throngs a place
- {報道陣|ほうどうじん}を{前|まえ}に: in front of the assembled press
- {報道陣|ほうどうじん}に{公開|こうかい}する: to open (something) to the press

SIMILAR WORDS:
- マスコミ: the mass media — the industry and its outlets, not the reporters physically present
- {記者団|きしゃだん}: the group of reporters — narrower, writers only, common in political coverage
